artifacts.summary: 4-phase red-first plan fixing git-commit-scoped.sh's V2 gate to classify already-staged deletions and decouple the git add pathspec set from the git commit set.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell script validates pathspecs before a git add + git commit pair, the two invocations need SEPARATE pathspec sets, not one shared array. An already-staged deletion (git rm, or the delete half of git mv) is absent from both the working tree and the index, so it must be included in `git commit -- <paths>` (or the deletion is silently dropped from the commit) but MUST be excluded from `git add` (which exits 128 on such a path, and because git add is a single all-or-nothing invocation, one bad entry aborts staging for every other path in the batch). The correct existence test for this third class is `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>` guarded by `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`; a path added and removed within the same uncommitted session correctly falls through to the genuinely-unmatched branch. Generalizes to any pathspec-validating wrapper: match-vs-drop is a two-way classification that silently loses deletions; the correct shape is three-way.
